item: The repository's primary 2026 results feed has a stale Week-10 row
observation: nfl-desk-35a1feb2/data/results_feed_2026.csv holds 150 rows; the row for the Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens, game id 2026_10_LAC_BAL, has blank scores and the status SCHEDULED - NOT KICKED OFF AT READ TIME. The official nfl.com Week-10 schedule page, read on 2026-11-19, shows that game as FINAL on Monday 16 November, Chargers 23, Ravens 20. The official league standings include the game. A per-club reconciliation of the feed against the standings therefore fails for exactly two clubs: Baltimore reads 4 wins and 6 losses in the standings against 4 and 5 in the feed, and Los Angeles Chargers reads 1 and 8 against 0 and 8. Every other club, and all 13 other Week-10 finals, agree exactly.
decision_impact: Any backtest, rating fit or availability join that reads this feed will mis-state the Week-10 result for two clubs, and therefore mis-state the ratings and the two clubs' season records.
action: A cross-session request has been logged on COORDINATION.md for the owning session. This desk publishes a corrected 150-game feed in its own namespace, reconciled to the standings with 0 mismatches, and does not edit the owning session's file.

item: No market price source is admitted, so no market line, residual, closing-line value or return exists
observation: The price store holds 39 model-record rows with every opening and closing cell blank. The leaderboard's staking column cannot be filled, the real-price return is undefined, and the joint-evidence gate cannot be satisfied because the operator's void and push rules are unknown.
decision_impact: Nothing about money can be computed or ranked. Every money-related cell is blank and labelled, and the gates that depend on it are marked BLOCKED rather than failed.
action: Decide the price-data policy first. See SG-A59-01, which states the options, the recommendation and what would change it.

item: Four other repository results feeds are shorter than the true 2026 corpus
observation: nfl-market-desk and nfl-desk-e46fb855 hold 145 games each and are missing five of the fourteen Week-10 games; nfl-c98c6270 holds 150 rows but leaves the Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals row out entirely and leaves the Chargers at Ravens row as NOT FINAL; nfl-command-desk holds 150 rows but is missing the Rams at Cardinals row; nfl-price-results-853c0074 holds 136 games and is missing all fourteen Week-10 games.
decision_impact: Any desk that reads one of these shorter feeds will compute on an incomplete corpus. The number of games in the corpus is verifiable: the official standings sum to 149 wins and 2 ties, which is 150 games.
action: Logged as a cross-session request. The canonical corpus used by this desk is its own 150-row feed, reconciled against the standings with 0 mismatches.

item: The earlier Week-11 availability read in the repository is a game-page sample, not a league report
observation: data/nfl-desk-f2e20e96/availability_wk11_preview.csv holds 10 rows read at 2026-11-18T03:46Z from two game pages, which expose four rows per club. It carries club statements that Minnesota and San Francisco have no active injuries. The full league report, read at 2026-11-19T06:45Z, names 10 Minnesota rows and 15 San Francisco rows, including Minnesota receiver Jordan Addison, who did not participate.
decision_impact: A game page is not an availability source. The delta between the two reads is published in this desk so the change is visible rather than the level.
action: The delta table is published with both read clocks on every row.

item: The depth-order source is verified for 31 of 32 clubs only
observation: nfl-desk-e46fb855/data/depth_slots.csv records 702 rows across 32 clubs. Thirty clubs are marked parsed. Houston is a single row marked NOT PARSED because the club publishes the depth chart as an image with no text table. The Patriots carry 19 parsed rows and 7 rows marked as a partial capture. A second capture in nfl-c98c6270 holds 890 rows across 32 clubs with Houston as a single image_only row, 14 shared rank-1 slots and 5 empty first strings.
decision_impact: The backup-deficiency feature, the off-versus-defence matchup matrix and the starters-out count all depend on a complete depth order, and are therefore blocked and left blank.
action: Route (b), the official Game Book, is proven on one game and is the better long-term source because it publishes who actually started. See SG-A59-02.

item: The availability graph covers one game, not a league dataset
observation: The official NFL Game Book for Washington at New York, Week 10, was read in full on 2026-11-19. It publishes the starting lineups, the substitutions, the players who did not play, the Not Active list and the game-day weather and surface line. No capture job exists to run it across the league.
decision_impact: The expected-versus-actual starter comparison cannot be treated as a dataset until the Game Book route is run over the whole evaluation window.
action: The single game is published as a proof of route, with every line source-linked.

item: No official snap-count source was verified, so route (b) for depth is unproven
observation: The official Game Book was read in full and contains no snap count. The official Next Gen Stats glossary was read on 2026-11-19 and publishes tracking metrics, including time to throw, completion probability and separation, and does not document a public per-player snap series.
decision_impact: The brief requires that depth be modelled from playing time. Until an official play-time source is verified, the depth feature stays unbuilt rather than approximated.
action: Recorded as the open prerequisite for the depth-order decision.

item: The three blank Lions game-status cells are a publication-timing fact, not a parsing failure
observation: Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays and D.J. Reed appear on the official Week-11 injury report with a blank game-status cell, read at 2026-11-19T06:45Z. The Lions play at Tampa Bay on Sunday 22 November. The same three players were listed Out on the official Week-10 report. The Sunday game-status columns are simply not yet published at the time of this read.
decision_impact: Nothing. Filling those cells would be inference, and the brief forbids it.
action: The cells stay blank and are flagged as the publisher's timing, not a defect.

item: No durable snapshot store, scheduler, freshness monitor or drift alarm exists
observation: The capture log records a read clock and the SHA-256 of the stored extract for one capture, but there is no append-only store outside the static site, no scheduled job and no alarm on a source or schema change.
decision_impact: The multi-day availability series cannot be replayed as it was known, so a point-in-time backtest of availability is not yet possible.
action: Raised as SG-A59-06 in the suggestions register and recorded against the affected requirements.

item: Two official venue strings differ for the same fixture
observation: The official game centre for the Colts at Texans prints HOUSTON, TX and RELIANT STADIUM. The schedule page for the same fixture links a hotel at NRG Stadium. Both are official NFL strings for the same building.
decision_impact: A venue key that is not consistent across rows will break any stadium or weather feature joined on the venue name.
action: The game-centre string is used, and the conflict is published rather than silently resolved. See question Q-A59-10.

item: The official schedule-release landing page carries no publication date
observation: The 2026 NFL Schedule Release page was read on 2026-11-19. It publishes the schedule, the nine international games with their venues and dates, and the flexible-scheduling notice for Weeks 16, 17 and 18. It prints no announcement date, and the page carries no visible date stamp.
decision_impact: The dated announcement requirement cannot be satisfied from this page alone, so the date cell is left blank rather than guessed.
action: Raised as question Q-A59-11, which asks for a dated official source.
